newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid Hussain up on restructuring talk.
newsitem.headline: Rashid Hussain up on restructuring talk.

text.p: Shares of Malaysian stockbroking group Rashid Hussain Bhd rose 6.31 percent on Friday amid speculation of a restructuring at the company, traders and analysts said.
Jupiter Securities, in a research note on Friday, said there was talk that Rashid has sold 20 percent of its stake to Morgan Stanley Group Inc at 12.00 ringgit a share.

A Rashid spokesman said he was not aware of the rumoured development. "At this point I don't have any information" on the matter, he said when contacted. A Morgan Stanley spokesman said he had no confirmation of the talk.
The Morgan Stanley spokesman, based at the company's Hong Kong office, said, "At this point, we have not purchased a 20 percent stake in Rashid Hussain."
At the end of the morning session, the stock was up 70 cents to 11.80 on heavy volume of 3.73 million shares traded. It hit a new year-high of 11.90 earlier.
Traders said there was also speculation of a restructuring involving Rashid and its 20 percent-owned financial group, DCB Holdings Bhd.
DCB stock rose 30 cents to 8.20 on volume of 605,000 shares traded. DCB officials could not be immediately contacted.
